title: Cross-functional lane protocols and rapid escalation playbook for release readiness
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight, operational playbook that standardizes 'lanes' for cross-functional dependency readiness during quarter and release handoffs. Each lane is a compact readiness contract (signals + OWNER + SLAs) between Product, Engineering, Design, Security, and Infra so teams can surface, reconcile, and resolve blockers with predictable escalation paths. The playbook should be usable for both planned feature rollouts and unplanned hotfix windows, and integrate with the Console readiness dashboard and Alerts channel.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Lane templates (Green/Amber/Red) documented with required readiness signals and owner actions
A2: Escalation flow defined with SLA timers and on-call roles for each lane
A3: Automation hooks defined for Console dashboard to surface lane status from tickets and CI jobs
A4: Pilot completed with two feature teams and retro captured, showing reduced late-stage blockers by >= 30% for the pilot scope
A5: Playbook published to Confluence and linked from squad kickoff checklist
decisions: D1: Use three-line lane model (Green/Amber/Red) instead of numeric readiness score to keep ops simple for cross-team consumers
D2: Primary escalation path starts with lane owner -> PM -> Eng on-call -> Security lead -> Head of Infra; alternate path via SRE rotation for infra emergencies
D3: Console will show lane status pulled from ticket labels + CI gates; we will not require custom APIs in pilot (use GitHub checks and labeling)
tradeoffs: T1: Simpler lane model reduces granularity of risk but increases adoption speed across teams
T2: Relying on ticket labels and GitHub checks avoids early engineering work but can surface false positives until automation matures
T3: Tighter SLAs for escalation shorten response time but increase interrupt cost for small P2 work
